question: Does the smallest operator that acts below the invariant boundary scale—an exact one-hole contextual lift of a valid source instance at a proper subterm of a minimum boundary endpoint—strictly contract the separation-8 residual?

operator.name: BOUNDARY_CONTEXT_LIFT
operator.scope: Only minimum cross-component boundary endpoints of the frozen post-contractor 0036 state.
operator.construction: Choose a proper subterm u of a boundary endpoint T, match either source side to u, instantiate remaining source variables from the frozen L1 fill pool, obtain the valid source equality u=v, and lift that equality through exactly the one-hole context T=C[u] to produce C[u]=C[v].
operator.proof_requirement: Every accepted contextual edge must be represented by a source-instance proof node followed only by symmetry when required and the exact chain of congruence nodes induced by the one-hole context; a strict contractor counts only if replay_dag accepts the resulting target closure when closure occurs.
operator.isolation: Direct source and intermediate congruence proof nodes are proof-only; only the final context-lifted equality is admitted as a graph edge for scoring.

decision_rule.BOUNDARY_CONTEXT_LIFT_CONTRACTS: At least one valid context-lifted source consequence reduces cross-component separation below 8; report the best contraction and whether applying it yields replayable closure.
decision_rule.BOUNDARY_CONTEXT_LIFT_EXHAUSTED: All bounded context-lifted source consequences satisfying the frozen protocol leave separation at least 8.
decision_rule.MEASUREMENT_FAILURE: Frozen parent facts or the prospectively observed plateau invariant fail to reproduce, or a purported proof object fails replay when closure is claimed.

notes: This protocol is committed before the executable. It attacks only the invariant-supported granularity obstruction; it does not inspect or tune against any sealed transfer case.
